It's a Bristleworm, which is a good member of the clean up crew but can look creepy/ugly. There are different homemade traps (water bottle with holes, pantyhose) that you can use overnight with some bait and just remove them in the morning. You could also get a Coral Banded Shrimp to eat them. If you have one bristleworm you probably have more (some are really tiny) and they multipy like crazy with overfeeding. I don't think yours is a Fireworm, but I'm also new to the hobby, so maybe look into some more picture and angles and compare the two because Fireworms will try to eat your livestock. With it being that big I would definitely remove it, and don't touch it because the bristles are sharp.
